conc.title: Park the task, not the thread.
conc.lede: spawn puts a green task on a pool with one worker per core. Sockets, sleeps, channels and locks park the task and hand the thread back. There is no async, no await and no second colour of function: code that looks blocking stays simple.
conc.tick_1: 10,000 tasks that each sleep 100 ms finish in about 0.5 s on a laptop.
conc.tick_2: Preempted when a task spins past its slice, so one hot loop cannot starve a worker.
conc.tick_3: TLS and DNS park too. Handshakes run on the reactor; lookups on their own thread.
conc.tick_4: A precise, generational GC with a write barrier and a verifier mode in CI.
conc.sched_parked: tasks: parked, cost a queue slot
conc.caption: Thousands of parked tasks, a handful of threads. A task that wakes goes back on a queue; a free worker picks it up.
agents.title: Cheap to learn. Cheap to correct.
agents.lede: An agent spends its tokens reading docs, choosing between options and retrying after errors. slang is designed to cut all three, for the agent and for whoever reviews its work.
agents.learn_text: llms-small.txt is the language and its packages on one page, about 3k tokens. Every example in it compiles in CI. For a single API, ask the compiler.
agents.errors_text: A compile error names the construct, the line and what to write instead. A runtime error names the function and the values, so the next attempt is the right one.
agents.errors_bar: one turn to fix, not five
agents.quiet_text: Tool output an agent can afford: one line when the tests pass, and only the failures when they do not.
agents.bench_text: Five backend tasks went to the same agent across four stacks (one run each). Every stack passed 5/5 hidden acceptance tests. slang used the fewest lines (705 LOC vs. 922–1,705) and stayed lean in memory (9.6 MB RSS at 46.2k req/s), but still spent more total cached input tokens (765k) because frontier models are not pretrained on slang or zokor yet.

syntax.title: Familiar on purpose. Small on purpose.
syntax.read_text: fn, guard let, switch, chan: shapes from Go and Swift, because people and models already know them. Every novelty costs someone a retry.
syntax.left_text: Each missing feature is one less way for a program to surprise you.
syntax.no_exceptions_desc: result[T, E] for bad data, fault for a bad world
syntax.no_closures_desc: A function value is a C function pointer. Nothing is captured
syntax.no_interfaces_desc: Generics, checked for each type they are used with
syntax.c_title: C is the runtime, not a foreign country
syntax.c_text: slang emits C and hands it to your cc. Calling a C library is extern fn and a linker flag: no bindings generator, no marshalling layer, no second build system.

faq.title: Asked, answered.
faq.a_prod: It is young: v0.2, and the language can still change. The runtime is tested on three platforms on every merge, including a collector verifier and stress runs under forced preemption. Read Known limitations before you bet a service on it, and pin a commit when you do.
faq.q_fast: Is it faster than Go or Rust?
faq.a_fast: On what has been measured so far: it uses less memory than Go, finishes the CPU and allocation job in two thirds of Go's time, and trails Rust. Raw HTTP throughput is within a few percent of both. The heavier database-and-JSON tier has not run yet. The benchmarks page shows every number, including the ones slang loses.
faq.a_c: C runs everywhere a server does, its compilers have decades of optimisation in them, and every C library is one extern fn away. slangc emits one C file with the runtime spliced in and builds it with cc -O3 -flto.
faq.q_missing: Why no closures, exceptions or null?
faq.a_missing: Each is a place where control flow or ownership hides. Without closures a function value is exactly a C function pointer and the collector can ignore it. Without exceptions every failure is a value you can see in the signature. Without null, absence is opt[T] and the compiler makes you handle it.
faq.q_cheap: What does "cheap for agents" mean, and is it proven?
faq.a_cheap: It means fewer tokens to learn the language, fewer choices to reason about, and errors that lead to the fix in one turn. The first published agent benchmark run above shows slang using the fewest lines of code (705 LOC vs. 922–1,705) with 5/5 passing and 9.6 MB RSS at 46.2k req/s; total cached input tokens are still higher today only because frontier models are not pretrained on slang or zokor yet.
faq.q_ffi: Can I call existing C libraries?
faq.a_ffi: Yes: extern fn plus link "name". Numbers, bool, str, bytes and opaque pointers cross the boundary; GC-managed values are rejected at compile time, so C never sees their layout.
